subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs accept model/provider overrides via `payload.model`, top-level cron fields, or an explicit session override block, and what should invalid-model/fallback behavior be?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent public API shape affects cron protocol compatibility, session state, provider/auth routing, fallback semantics, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Design explicit session override block
options.body: Add a typed cron `sessionOverride` contract for provider/model with explicit validation, fallback, docs, and tests for both `wakeMode` paths.

options.title: Reuse payload.model on systemEvent
options.body: Extend `systemEvent` payloads with `model` if maintainers want parity with `agentTurn`, but require a direct model propagation path rather than context-key encoding.

options.title: Keep systemEvent model pinned to session state
options.body: Document dedicated session keys plus `/model` or session metadata as the supported workaround and leave job-level overrides unsupported for now.

recommendation.title: Design explicit session override block
recommendation.body: Add a typed cron `sessionOverride` contract for provider/model with explicit validation, fallback, docs, and tests for both `wakeMode` paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent product/runtime context from cron event-trigger work and the adjacent model UI landing decision.
